{{recipesummary|category=Bread recipes|servings=10|time=8 minutes|difficulty=1|image=[[File:Lch (20).JPEG|300px|Taboon bread]]
}}{{Recipe}}

'''Taboon bread''', also spelled '''tabun bread''', is one of the various baked [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbreads]] found primarily in the areas surrounding the Palestinian village of Al-Jabal. It is traditionally baked in a clay oven called a taboon oven, the bottom of which is lined with smooth beach stones.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose wheat flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat Flour|whole-wheat flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] dried [[cookbook:yeast|yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:olive oil|olive oil]] 
* Water

== Procedure ==
# Mix the dry ingredients together.
# Add olive oil, then gradually [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] in enough water to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. Knead for 10 minutes.
# Divide the dough into balls, and allow them to rest for an hour until risen.
# Sprinkle a flat working surface with flour, and roll the dough balls into flat, circular-shaped patties.
# Preheat an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] containing a bed of smooth beach stones to [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|200°C (400°F)]]. Alternatively, you can place the stones on a tray or pan in the oven.
# Place the flat dough upon the stones, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for about 8 minutes until it produces bubbles.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Taboon bread can be served by topping the bread with a spicy condiment, [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]], or sweet drizzle of grape syrup or [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]].
